extracted.intended_audience: administrators, legal counsel, and compliance officers at institutions of higher education (Title IX practitioners)
extracted.subtask_short: Title IX regulatory compliance for IHEs
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for institutions of higher education on which Title IX regulations to follow and practical next steps after a federal court struck down the 2024 Final Rule and reverted regulatory obligations to the 2020 Final Rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reversion to 2020 Final Rule (Tennessee v. Cardona)
rubrics_metrics.description: The U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Kentucky struck down the 2024 Final Rule and reverted regulatory expectations to the 2020 Final Rule, which now applies nationwide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IHEs should begin preparing to re-implement Title IX policies that comply with the 2020 Final Rule, since the court found the 2024 Final Rule 'off the books' and the 2020 Final Rule again controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency lacked authority to expand Title IX to include 'gender identity'
rubrics_metrics.description: The court held that the Department of Education lacked the authority to expand the definition of Title IX to prohibit discrimination on the basis of 'gender identity.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The court reasoned that by including 'gender identity' the 2024 Final Rule made Title IX's prevention of discrimination based on sex 'largely meaningless,' and thus exceeded agency authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bostock analogy insufficient for Title IX rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: The Biden administration argued the 2024 Final Rule should be upheld by analogizing to the Supreme Court's Bostock decision, but the court rejected that analogy for Title IX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The court distinguished Bostock (which expanded protections under Title VII for transgender faculty and staff) from Title IX, relying on the plain text of the Title IX statute to find Bostock did not automatically extend the same protections to students under Title IX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arbitrary and capricious due to inconsistent rules about sex separation
rubrics_metrics.description: The court found the 2024 Final Rule 'arbitrary and capricious' insofar as it created inconsistencies about when separation of sexes was permissible under Title IX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example inconsistencies noted by the court include permitting sex separation in fraternity and sorority living facilities but not permitting it with respect to bathroom facilities; such inconsistencies supported the arbitrary-and-capricious finding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Likely First Amendment violation regarding compelled use of names/pronouns
rubrics_metrics.description: The court found the 2024 Final Rule likely violated the First Amendment by potentially requiring the use of names and pronouns associated with individuals’ gender identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The court reasoned that mandating such usage could chill speech or compel affirmation of beliefs with which a speaker disagrees, contributing to the rule's invalidation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inseparability of challenged provisions — entire 2024 Final Rule vacated
rubrics_metrics.description: The court concluded the challenged provisions of the 2024 Final Rule are too interwoven to be extricated from the rest of the rule, effectively taking the 2024 Final Rule 'off the books.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the provisions were found inseparable, institutions cannot rely on portions of the 2024 Final Rule and instead must follow the prior (2020) rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revise institutional Title IX policies to comply with the 2020 Final Rule
rubrics_metrics.description: IHEs that implemented changes in response to the 2024 Final Rule should revise Title IX policies and procedures to align with the 2020 Final Rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the primary recommended action item: update internal policies and procedures promptly so institutional practice matches the now-controlling 2020 regulatory framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Update all public and internal materials to reflect 2020 compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure all other materials (e.g., publications, handbooks, websites) are updated accordingly to reflect compliance with the 2020 Final Rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions should audit and revise student handbooks, webpages, training materials, and any published policies that had been changed to follow the 2024 Final Rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Train faculty, staff, and students on 2020-compliant policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide training to faculty, staff, and students on policies and procedures that comply with the 2020 Final Rule and how those policies apply to their roles and studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizations should refresh training programs and communications so that personnel understand investigatory, grievance, and nondiscrimination procedures as governed by the 2020 regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate potential new rulemaking under incoming administration
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the 2024 Final Rule was struck down and the incoming administration will not appeal, the incoming Department of Education leadership may swiftly propose new Title IX regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipated proposed changes could include revising definitions to specify only two genders/sexes and limiting transgender athletes' ability to participate on teams that reflect their gender identity; institutions should monitor rulemaking and be prepared to adapt.
